chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said:

I asked him: 'A female slave, her master had intercourse with her, then he decided to marry her off. What is the status of her child?' He said: 'She is of the same status, unless her husband stipulates otherwise.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to mean that if her husband is a slave to other people, then her children will be slaves to her master, unless the master of the slave stipulates otherwise. And if the intended one was free, then the children would be attached to him, according to what we have previously stated.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to a slave woman after her master marries her off?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that this ruling specifically applies when the husband is a slave to other masters, in which case the offspring remain slaves of the original master unless stipulated otherwise; if the husband were free, the children would follow his lineage. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'taba'iyyah' (subordination) in manumission contexts, where the status of the mother and the specific conditions of her marriage determine the legal standing of the progeny within the master's property.
